transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn Park (CEO), Marcus Li (CTO), Sara Gomez (VP Product), Daniel Kim (Head Eng), Lina Torres (Head Sales), Jordan Miles (Head People), plus company-wide all-hands

Summary (spoken):
[00:00] Evelyn Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick note we wanted to keep this tight, about an hour, lots to cover. Q3 was strong, we've seen continued growth on Hosted API and initial traction for Dedicated. I will hand off to Marcus for the tech highlights.

Product & Tech:
[05:12] Marcus Li: Thanks Evelyn. Quick wins: we've reduced median generation latency by ~12% on common seq lengths with the new kernel selector, and average cost per token dropped 8% with adaptive batching. These are real, customers are seeing it in logs, though there are a couple of edge cases at long sequences.
[07:45] Marcus Li: On Private, we've got a first on-prem pilot in final testing, still ironing out KMS/HSM integration and network cutovers — some of the issues are around cert rotation timings.
[09:20] Audience (Speaker 1): Quick question — is the latency improvement universal across all models?
[09:35] Marcus Li: Not universal; bigger gains on decoder-only and our quantized flows. Some encoder-decoder variants need more tuning.

Product Roadmap:
[12:00] Sara Gomez: High level roadmap: Dedicated improvements (autoscaling policies, burst capacity control), Private GA (beta customers in Nov), and Redwood Optimize features — model suggestions and automated batching profiles. We'll share the deck after this.
[14:10] Sara Gomez: Important note: Optimize will include quality monitoring tied to eval sets, so we can detect regressions faster — think of it as automated guardrails.

Business & GTM:
[18:30] Lina Torres: From sales, Q3 bookings up 27% Q/Q. Dedicated deals are longer sales cycles but higher ACV. We're iterating on a pricing matrix to make pilot-to-Dedicated transitions smoother.
[20:05] Lina Torres: We heard concerns from some accounts about price vs latency tradeoffs — we'll be offering a workshop for top 20 customers to walk through configs and quantify unit economics.

Security & Compliance:
[23:40] Daniel Kim: Security update: SOC 2 readiness is on track, working through evidence gathering. ISO exploratory work started with consultant; timeline looks like SOC 2 report by Q1 next year assuming no major gaps. Audit logs and RBAC enhancements are prioritized.
[25:00] Audience (Speaker 2): What's the plan for data residency?
[25:20] Jordan Miles: We'll have region controls for Hosted and Dedicated; Private obviously supports on-prem and VPC isolation for regulated customers.

People & Hiring:
[28:00] Jordan Miles: Hiring update — we're opening 18 roles across infra, product, and SRE. Focused hiring for kernel devs and reliability engineers. We're also piloting a new interview loop to speed decisions.
[30:10] Audience (Speaker 3): Any org changes?
[30:25] Evelyn Park: No structural reorganizations right now; just priorities shifting to support Dedicated and Private demand.

Customer Highlights:
[33:00] Lina Torres: Notable wins: a fintech customer went live on Dedicated and reported 40% cost reduction due to prefix caching and quantized models; another health-tech pilot is evaluating Private for data residency.

Q&A (mixed attendees):
[38:00] Audience (Speaker 4): How do we measure success for Optimize?
[38:20] Sara Gomez: Key metrics: percent cost saved, latency delta, and regression alerts triggered per eval set. We'll have SLAs around alert fidelity.
[40:00] Audience (Speaker 5): Any thoughts on competitive positioning vs Anthropic/OpenAI?
[40:15] Evelyn Park: We lean into serving and economics: predictable latency, cost controls, and flexible deployment. Competitors have model upside; our win is operational predictability and tooling.

Operational Notes:
[44:00] Daniel Kim: Ops priorities: make autoscaling more predictable under burst traffic, improve fallback routing to avoid noisy neighbor effects, and finalize a default caching policy.
[46:30] Daniel Kim: We'll run a canary with synthetic traffic next week to validate the autoscaler adjustments.

Closing / Housekeeping:
[50:00] Evelyn Park: Quick reminders — submit any town hall questions in the #all-hands channel; Sara will post the deck and roadmap. We're doing an informal AMA next month focused on pricing and sales enablement.
[52:10] Jordan Miles: People ops note — open Q&A sessions for candidates; please refer referrals to the hiring channel.

Recap & Next Steps:
[55:00] Evelyn Park: Recap: share roadmap deck, schedule sales deep-dive, publish SOC 2 timeline, and engineering to post perf notes. Thanks everyone.
[56:15] Audience (Speaker 6): Thanks leadership!

Transcript notes: transcription is automated; some proper nouns and product names may be mis-typed (eg. kernel selector could be transcribed differently). There is occasional overlap and filler words not fully captured.
